as_told.title: Malmgren's hidden CIA ties and Paul Mellon's walking stick

plain: Michels argues, as his own reading, that Harold Malmgren, a former Washington official he interviewed, had quiet ties to the CIA from around 1960, and that his work for the Institute for Defense Analyses, a research group that works for the Pentagon, served as cover. Among his "fun facts": Malmgren told him he was best friends with Tom Farmer, who "happened to be the GC, the general counsel of the CIA," and Malmgren brought the walking stick of the financier Paul Mellon to the interview, which Michels held for half of it; Michels also points to Malmgren's diaries. If he is right, Malmgren stood much closer to the intelligence world than his public career suggests.
